key_insight: A physics-grounded digital twin can rapidly screen robotic in-space welding conditions and controller settings before costly flight-like experiments.
engineering_relevance: This framework helps de-risk on-orbit metal joining by combining thermal weld-pool physics, surrogate models, and manipulator control for process planning and autonomy.
method: Finite-volume thermal weld-pool model with solid-liquid phase change, thermocapillary transport, and local-pressure effects.
Gaussian-process and neural-network surrogates trained and validated with repeated five-fold cross-validation.
Simulated six-axis manipulator study with closed-loop control of synergic power during an L-shaped seam.
evidence_signal: Across repeated five-fold cross-validation, the GP outperformed the neural network on all eight outputs, and 74/80 held-out solver responses fell within nominal 90% GP predictive intervals.
watch_item: The results are simulation-based and still need thermal-vacuum, reduced-gravity, and hardware-in-the-loop validation before operational use.
paper_title: De-Risking Robotic Welding for In-Space Metal Joining Through Physics-Grounded Digital Twins
